lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding

nextStoryContext: US-R1-001 (CAM-388 review round 1) fixed the reviewer-flagged false-negative regression in stripQuotedSpans (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts): the closing-quote search used bare command.indexOf(ch, i+1) with two real gaps -- (a) an unterminated quote fell back to end=command.length, swallowing the rest of the command into a discarded span, and (b) the POSIX '\'' single-quote-escape idiom (close, backslash-escaped literal quote, reopen) fooled the naive search into treating each embedded segment of a multi-segment -c payload as its own independent (non-wrapper) quoted span, discarding every segment after the first, including the one carrying the real comparison. Fix: a new findClosingQuoteIndex(command, quoteChar, searchFrom) helper skips past a candidate closing ' immediately followed by the literal 3-char continuation \'' and keeps searching for the true close; stripQuotedSpans now treats closeIdx===-1 as literal text (append char, advance one) instead of swallowing to end-of-string. Two new fixture rows added to test/fixtures/oracle-lint/oracle-lint-cases.txt reproducing the reviewer's exact two verified regressions (both now correctly flag): the escaped-idiom sh -c wrapper, and the unterminated-quote printf case. Verified by hand-simulation (char-by-char index trace) and by bun test (58/58 pass, oracle-lint-cases.txt fixture-matrix test included). Confirmed against the live GNU Bash manual that the escape idiom's semantics ('a single quote may not occur between single quotes, even when preceded by a backslash'; workaround is close/escape/reopen) match the fix's assumptions. Full check:all spine green at this commit (test, embed-vendor, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps). scripts/cam/prd.json shows an unstaged reviewer-authored diff (US-R1-001/US-R1-002 stories plus a review block) that pre-existed this session's start and was deliberately left untouched/uncommitted per the 'do not edit prd.json' rule -- the supervisor owns that file. A second reviewer finding, US-R1-002 (isDashCWrapper's -c match is not scoped to a shell-interpreter word, so a non-interpreter -c payload like grep -c '...' or npx tool -c '...' gets unwrapped and scanned as live shell; not a regression, main already does this, but an uncorrected instance of the false-positive class CAM-388 exists to close), is queued next in prd.json and untouched by this story.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed no escape mechanism exists inside single quotes and that the close/escape/reopen idiom is the standard workaround for embedding a literal quote -- matches the fix's findClosingQuoteIndex continuation logic exactly.
